title: All-Inclusive Holidays in Poreč 2027: Hotels & Prices
metaDescription: Poreč does have all-inclusive hotels. See which resorts sell it, what is included, 2027 price ranges vs half-board and apartments, and who it suits.
content:
## Are There Real All-Inclusive Hotels in Poreč?

Yes. Poreč is one of the few places in Croatia with several genuine all-inclusive hotels. Most belong to two operators: Valamar and Plava Laguna. Current offers confirm all-inclusive at these properties:

- **Isabella Island Hotel & Villas (Valamar Collection)** on Sveti Nikola island, a short boat ride from the old town. All-inclusive is built into the rates.
- **Pical Family Hotel (Valamar Collection)**, a beachfront 5* family hotel marketed as all-inclusive. The neighbouring Pical Hotel sells half-board, so check which building you are booking.
- **Valamar Tamaris Resort** in the Lanterna area, where an all-inclusive plan is built around the Agava buffet restaurant.
- **Hotel Albatros Plava Laguna** in Zelena Laguna, a 4* hotel about 100 m from the beach.
- **Hotel Zorna Plava Laguna**, a 3* hotel in the same area.

Nearby, the **Maistra Select Funtana All Inclusive Resort** in Funtana (about 7 km north) is the best-rated option in the Poreč region.

All-inclusive here is seasonal. Resort operators typically run it from early May to mid-October, so a winter search will show half-board or breakfast only.

## What Is Usually Included

Packages differ by hotel, but the standard formula is:

- Breakfast, lunch and dinner as buffets, often with show cooking and themed evenings.
- Snacks and ice cream in the afternoon.
- Local house wine, beer, soft drinks, water and coffee at set hours, at the restaurant and at one or more bars.
- Pools, a kids' club and an animation programme.
- Light sports and activities such as mini golf, bike rental and a games room.

Most of the following usually cost extra: sun loungers and umbrellas at the beach, beach-bar drinks, water sports, spa treatments, premium spirits and à la carte restaurants. Excursions such as dolphin boat trips from the resort dock are charged separately, around €30 per person at Funtana. Hotels also charge a daily tourist tax (a few euros per adult) that may not be in the headline price.

## Price Per Person Per Night: Peak vs Shoulder Season

These are rough 2027 planning ranges for two adults sharing a double room. Exact rates depend on room type, dates and how early you book.

| Option | Shoulder (May–June, September) | Peak (mid-July to August) |
|---|---|---|
| All-inclusive, 3*–4* (Zorna, Albatros, Tamaris) | €60–90 | €90–130 |
| All-inclusive, upper end (Isabella Island, Pical, Funtana) | €90–130 | €140–200+ |
| Half-board, 4* hotel | €45–70 | €70–110 |
| Private apartment, room only | €20–35 | €35–60 |
| Apartment plus own food (shops, a few restaurant meals) | €45–65 | €60–90 |

The gap that matters is the last row. A private apartment with groceries and one restaurant dinner every two or three days usually costs 25–40% less than 4* all-inclusive in peak weeks. In shoulder season the gap narrows to €10–25 per person per day, which is why May, June and September are the best value for all-inclusive.

## All-Inclusive vs Half-Board vs Apartment

Half-board (breakfast and dinner) costs about 20–30% less than all-inclusive and leaves lunch and drinks to you. In Poreč this makes sense if you spend days in the old town, at Aquacolors water park or on excursions to Rovinj and Pula.

An apartment gives space, a kitchen and a flexible schedule. It carries no resort pool, kids' club or evening programme, so you must plan every day yourself.

## Who All-Inclusive Suits in Poreč

**Families with small children (roughly ages 2–10).** This is the strongest case. Meals at fixed hours, a kids' club, pools and early-evening entertainment remove daily decisions. Children's drinks and snacks are included, and a hotel base is easier with a nap schedule. Pical and Isabella Island are built specifically for this.

**Short stays of 3–5 nights.** You skip shopping, cooking and finding restaurants, and you use the package fully from the first day.

**Groups who want a fixed budget.** Drinks, snacks and meals are covered, so daily spending is predictable.

## Who Should Self-Cater Instead

- Couples and adults without children who want to eat in konobas in the old town.
- Stays of 10 days or more, when buffet food gets repetitive.
- Families with teenagers who will spend the day away from the hotel.
- Anyone who dislikes set meal times or a busy pool area.
- Light drinkers, who pay for drinks they do not use.

**Opinion:** Poreč's most expensive all-inclusive brands are not worth paying peak rates for unless children are the priority. In August, the 4* Albatros or Tamaris gives you the same buffet-and-pool formula for much less than Isabella Island or Pical. A Zelena Laguna or Lanterna all-inclusive in June is better value than any August package.

## Local Tips

- Isabella Island is on an island, so you are reliant on the shuttle boat. Check timetables if you plan to eat in town in the evenings.
- Albatros and Zorna are in Zelena Laguna, about 5 km south of the old town. Without a car, plan for the local tourist train or a taxi.
- Check whether beach loungers are included. At most resorts they are not.
- Look at "all-inclusive light" versions. Some hotels offer a reduced plan with fewer bar hours, which saves money.
- Book early. Valamar and Plava Laguna early-booking discounts are noticeably lower than last-minute rates.

## Nearest All-Inclusive Alternatives Outside Poreč

- **Funtana (about 7 km):** Maistra Select Funtana All Inclusive Resort.
- **Umag (about 35 km north):** Hotel Aurora Plava Laguna, a main all-inclusive in Umag.
- **Rabac (east coast, about 70 km):** Valamar Bellevue Resort, Girandella Resort and Sunny Rabac.
- **Medulin (south of Pula):** TUI Blue Medulin; Pula itself has no all-inclusive hotels.
- **Rovinj:** Amarin family resort from Maistra.

faq.question: Does Poreč have all-inclusive hotels?
faq.answer: Yes. Isabella Island, Pical Family Hotel, Valamar Tamaris Resort, Hotel Albatros and Hotel Zorna all sell all-inclusive in or next to Poreč. Maistra Select Funtana All Inclusive Resort is about 7 km away.

faq.question: How much does all-inclusive cost per person in Poreč?
faq.answer: Roughly €60–90 per person per night in shoulder season and €90–160 in peak, for two adults sharing a room. The upper-end Valamar resorts can exceed €200 per person in August.

faq.question: Is all-inclusive cheaper than half-board in Poreč?
faq.answer: No. All-inclusive costs about 20–30% more than half-board at the same hotel. It pays off only if you will eat lunch and drink at the hotel.

faq.question: Is all-inclusive in Poreč good for families with small children?
faq.answer: Yes, it is the best fit. Kids' clubs, pools, fixed meal times and entertainment are included, particularly at Pical Family Hotel and Isabella Island.

faq.question: When is all-inclusive available in Poreč?
faq.answer: Mainly from early May to mid-October. Most hotels switch to half-board or breakfast outside that season.

faq.question: Is a private apartment cheaper than all-inclusive in Poreč?
faq.answer: Usually yes, especially in peak season when you cook some meals yourself. Expect roughly €45–90 per person per night with food, against €90–160 for all-inclusive.

quickAnswer: Yes, Poreč has real all-inclusive hotels: Isabella Island, Pical Family Hotel, Valamar Tamaris, Hotel Albatros and Hotel Zorna (Plava Laguna), plus Maistra Select Funtana nearby. Expect roughly €60–90 per person per night in shoulder season and €90–160 in peak, with half-board and apartments cheaper.
